viewsContainer.packageHub.title: PackageHub
view.packageHubExplorer.name: Package Health
config.dashboardViewMode.description: Dashboard layout: list, by project, or by package.
config.scanOnStartup.description: Scan packages when the workspace opens.
config.includePrerelease.description: Include prereleases in the next outdated list. Off by default. The vulnerability scan is unchanged. Applied on the next scan.
config.minimumSeverity.description: Lowest severity PackageHub reports. Does not change NuGetAuditLevel in the project.
config.minimumReleaseAge.description: How many days old a latest version must be before it is preferred. 0 is off. Highest patch ignores this. Publish dates come from the local NuGet cache; with packageHub.onlineLookups off, a date that is not cached is reported as unknown.
config.ignoredPackages.description: Package ids to hide from scan results.
welcome.noFolder:
PackageHub reads the NuGet packages in your C# and F# projects. Open a folder that contains a .csproj, .fsproj or .sln file to start.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
[Get Started](command:packageHub.openWalkthrough)
welcome.noProjects:
No .csproj, .fsproj or .sln file was found in this folder. Open a .NET project or solution and PackageHub scans it for you.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
[Scan Again](command:packageHub.scanWorkspace)
[Get Started](command:packageHub.openWalkthrough)
walkthrough.open.title: Open a .NET project or solution
walkthrough.open.description:
PackageHub starts when the folder has a `.csproj`, `.fsproj`, `.sln` or `Directory.Packages.props` file. C# and F# projects are both read.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
walkthrough.scan.title: Run your first scan
walkthrough.scan.description:
The scan starts a few seconds after the folder opens. You can also run it yourself. It uses `dotnet list package` for vulnerable, outdated and deprecated packages, and saving a project file scans again.
[Scan Workspace](command:packageHub.scanWorkspace)
walkthrough.marks.title: Read the line marks
walkthrough.marks.description: Open a project file or `Directory.Packages.props`. Each package line gets one mark: a warning for vulnerable, a cross and the newer version for outdated, a deprecated mark, or a check when the package is current. Hover the line for the details.
walkthrough.update.title: Apply a safe update from the lightbulb
walkthrough.update.description: Put the cursor on a vulnerable package and press **Ctrl+.** (**Cmd+.** on macOS). The first choice is the highest patch in the same major. Latest and the first fixed version come after it. Nothing is written until you choose **Yes, Update**.
walkthrough.health.title: Open Package Health and the dashboard
walkthrough.health.description:
The Package Health view lists vulnerable, outdated, deprecated and conflicting packages, and your projects. The Health Dashboard shows the totals and the bulk updates for highest patch and highest minor.
[Show Package Health](command:packageHubExplorer.focus)
[Show Health Dashboard](command:packageHub.showHealthDashboard)
walkthrough.why.title: Ask "Why is this here?"
walkthrough.why.description: Not sure where a package comes from? Choose **Why is this here?** from the hover, the tree or the right-click menu on a package line. A window shows the path from your project to the package. Needs the .NET SDK 8.0.400 or newer.
walkthrough.settings.title: Tune what you see
walkthrough.settings.description:
Hide low severities with `packageHub.minimumSeverity`, add prereleases to the outdated list with `packageHub.includePrerelease`, or wait a few days before a new latest version is preferred with `packageHub.minimumReleaseAge`.
[Open PackageHub Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22packageHub.%22)
walkthrough.title: Get started with PackageHub
walkthrough.description: Find vulnerable, outdated and deprecated NuGet packages in your C# and F# projects, and update them safely.
config.onlineLookups.markdownDescription: Allow PackageHub to contact nuget.org itself when local data is missing: advisory ranges (VulnerabilityInfo) and publish dates for `#packageHub.minimumReleaseAge#`. Off by default: PackageHub then makes no network request of its own. `dotnet` still uses your NuGet.config feeds as usual.
config.timeouts.listSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for dotnet list package (vulnerable, installed) and other quick dotnet commands.
config.timeouts.outdatedSeconds.descript: Timeout in seconds for dotnet list package --outdated and --deprecated.
config.timeouts.restoreSeconds.descripti: Timeout in seconds for dotnet restore and dotnet add package.
config.maxDotnetProcesses.description: How many dotnet processes PackageHub runs at the same time.
